headline: Top court keeps care going for transgender inmates.
summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to let the Trump administration enforce new medical restrictions on transgender people in federal prison. A lower court's block stays. The policy would halt surgeries, taper hormones and end makeup and wigs. About 600 inmates got hormone therapy in 2025. Alito and Thomas would have let it start.
cover_answer: Not for now. The judges said keep the treatment going.
table_question: Can a new boss cancel a rule everyone's followed for 30 years?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: In America, some people in prison take medicine from a doctor that helps them feel like themselves. The president wanted the prisons to stop giving it. Yesterday the top judges said no, keep going for now. Like a nurse who keeps your medicine going until the doctor says otherwise. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Medicine, a nurse, and a no. The word transgender can wait for the question.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them the medicine, the nurse who keeps it going and a president told no. Transgender waits for the question, because the ruling is about who decides. Expect "why did he want to stop it?" He said the government shouldn't pay for it. The judges said wait.

8-12.script: Trump ordered prisons to stop paying for treatment for transgender inmates. A judge blocked it: stopping the medicine can bring on depression and suicidal thoughts. The Supreme Court kept the block in place. A referee's whistle: play stops until the review ends.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out rules and whether adults apply them consistently, so the script runs the chain: an order, a judge's block, an appeal, a whistle. The referee's review is the mechanism, play stopped until the call is checked. Expect "so who wins?" Nobody yet. The order only says it can't start while the case goes on.

13-17.script: Should a prison stop a treatment it has given for 30 years because a new president says so? The administration says security; the inmates' lawyers say it has shown no evidence. Second: the court gave no reasons, and two justices would have let it start. What does a one-line order tell you?
13-17.why: Thirty years against one order, then a silent court.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: a president can set prison policy, and a court can stop him until the case is heard. The script sets 30 years of care against one order, then asks about the court's silence, a one-line order with no reasons. Expect "so is this the law now?" No. A pause. The lower courts decide the rest.

5-7.a: Someone who feels they're a different gender from what the doctor wrote down when they were born. Some take medicine to feel like themselves.

8-12.a: Not yet. A judge blocked it, and the Supreme Court kept the block.

8-12.q: Why did Trump want to stop it?
8-12.a: His order: no federal money for it. In court his lawyers said security.

13-17.a: No. The case goes on below; the policy can't start while it does.

13-17.q: Didn't the court ban this for kids?
13-17.a: It upheld Tennessee's ban for minors. Adult prisoners are a separate question.
